concerns.concern: A positive THz photoresistance only shows that resistivity depends on electron temperature. It does not show that electron–electron collisions relax the current. Other electron-temperature-only mechanisms (temperature-dependent impurity screening, thermal smearing of energy-dependent scattering or density of states, hydrodynamic/viscous corrections) could also give positive photoresistance and must be estimated quantitatively.
concerns.quote: Δρ_THz > 0 only shows that ρ depends on T_e, not that e–e collisions relax current.

concerns.concern: Electron–phonon scattering may itself depend on electron temperature, so phonons are not excluded. The Bloch–Grüneisen temperature is only a few kelvin, hot electrons up to ~17 K can spontaneously emit phonons, the enhanced coupling in phonon theories would amplify this, and hot-phonon bottlenecks could raise the effective phonon temperature.
concerns.quote: Electron–phonon scattering can itself depend on T_e in the relevant regime.

concerns.concern: The monolayer graphene control is not a valid null test for twisted bilayer graphene. It has weaker electron–phonon coupling, different absorbed power, cooling channels and Fermi temperature, and no electron-temperature calibration. It therefore cannot test the stronger coupling central to the phonon scenario.
concerns.quote: The MLG control is not a valid null test for TBG.

concerns.concern: The electron-temperature calibration is partly circular. It compares photoresistance with equilibrium ρ(T), which presupposes that resistivity depends only on electron temperature, the very hypothesis under test.
concerns.quote: That comparison presupposes ρ = ρ(T_e) only, which is the very hypothesis under test.

concerns.concern: In the linear-T regime there is no quantitative comparison of the electron-temperature derivative with the equilibrium slope. A simple estimate gives about 23% photoresistance, which is not obviously consistent with the headline 70%. The densities, temperatures and devices giving 70% must be specified and reconciled.
concerns.quote: This is not obviously consistent with the headline 70%, which is shown only in the Supplementary Information.

concerns.concern: Taking the zero-frequency limit of an optical-conductivity result may not give the dc resistivity. Momentum-conserving normal collisions leave a finite Drude weight in clean systems, so a proper derivation including disorder and stating validity conditions is required.
concerns.quote: a finite e–e contribution to dc ρ generally requires disorder and violates Matthiessen's rule

concerns.concern: The magic-angle conclusion lacks a mechanism. The inter-pocket theory gives T², not linear-in-T resistivity, so the claim to unify magic-angle and higher-angle transport is rhetorical.
concerns.quote: The "unification" is therefore rhetorical.

concerns.concern: The second calibration method, Shubnikov–de Haas damping, is done at finite magnetic field. There, absorption and cooling differ, possibly in a different device or at a different filling, and this is not shown in the main text.
concerns.quote: There, absorption and cooling differ (cyclotron and Bernstein resonances), possibly in a different device or at different ν

concerns.concern: Slow lattice or substrate (bolometric) heating that follows the 44.4 Hz modulation is not ruled out. No modulation-frequency dependence, on-chip lattice thermometry or absorbed-power estimate is given.
concerns.quote: No modulation-frequency dependence, on-chip lattice thermometry or absorbed-power estimate is given.

concerns.concern: The theory gives weak quantitative discrimination. The screening parameter Λ spans two orders of magnitude and is effectively a fit parameter.
concerns.quote: The "best correspondence Λ ≈ 0.2–0.3" is effectively a fit parameter.

concerns.concern: No dependence of the T² prefactor on filling, twist angle or gate distance is predicted and compared with the multiple available devices. The authors should show measured A(ν) against Eq. (1) using a continuum-model band structure at 1.58°.
concerns.quote: No dependence on ν, θ or gate distance is predicted and compared.

concerns.concern: The trigonal-warping amplitude is small exactly where the anomaly is claimed (ν≈0.1), where the pockets look nearly circular. It is unclear that warping is large enough there.
concerns.quote: The warping amplitude ∝ k_F a is small exactly where the anomaly is claimed (ν ≈ 0.1).

concerns.concern: The T² fits extend to ~T_F/2, beyond the validity of the low-temperature expansion. Thermally excited minority carriers undercut the claim that the system remains unipolar at all measured temperatures.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3b spans 10–100 K, reaching ~T_F/2, where the low-T expansion in Eq. (1) is not valid.

concerns.concern: Near ν=3.8, thermal activation across the ν=4 superlattice gap could cause electron–hole friction or drag mimicking T², and the gap size is not given.
concerns.quote: Near ν = 3.8, thermal activation across the ν = 4 superlattice gap could produce electron–hole friction or drag.

concerns.concern: Exponents extracted from log(ρ−ρ₀) depend sensitively on the choice of ρ₀. A local-exponent plot versus temperature and filling is needed.
concerns.quote: Exponents extracted from log(ρ − ρ₀) depend sensitively on the choice of ρ₀.

concerns.concern: The photoresistance data for the 1.58° device at ν≈0.1 are not shown, so the hot-electron and T² arguments may not refer to the same sample and filling.
concerns.quote: Δρ_THz for that device at ν ≈ 0.1 is not shown.

concerns.concern: The sublinear saturation of photoresistance with power is not modelled. Fitting a cooling-power law would test the hot-electron picture and yield an electron–phonon coupling that could be checked against a phonon-limited slope.
concerns.quote: The sublinear saturation of Δρ_THz(P) (Fig. 2d) is not modelled.

concerns.concern: Spatially nonuniform heating via antenna-connected contacts, hot spots and contact-resistance photoresponse are not discussed. Whether the measurement is two- or four-terminal is unclear.
concerns.quote: Hot spots near contacts and contact-resistance photoresponse are not discussed, and the probe geometry for Δρ_THz (two- versus four-terminal) is unclear.

concerns.concern: The umklapp kinematic thresholds assume isotropic Fermi pockets, despite the trigonal warping invoked later in the theory.
concerns.quote: The thresholds k_F > g/4√3 and k_F > g/4 assume isotropic pockets despite the warping invoked later.

concerns.concern: Novelty relative to prior hot-electron photoresistance studies of TBG (Hubmann et al.) is understated. Earlier work already used THz/IR photoresistance in TBG near the magic angle, including saturation with intensity.
concerns.quote: Hubmann et al. (Refs. 36–37) already used THz/IR photoresistance and photoconductance in TBG near the magic angle, including saturation with intensity.

concerns.concern: The claim of a "general framework" is not positioned relative to established hot-electron thermometry methods in graphene, such as noise thermometry and photothermoelectric methods.
concerns.quote: The "general framework" claim also needs positioning relative to established hot-electron thermometry in graphene (noise thermometry, photothermoelectric methods).

concerns.concern: The central 70% result and all electron-temperature calibrations are relegated to the Supplementary Information rather than the main figures.
concerns.quote: The central 70% result and all T_e calibrations are relegated to the Supplementary Information.

concerns.concern: There is no device table giving twist angle and its inhomogeneity, mobility, residual resistivity, dielectric thickness and geometry.
concerns.quote: There is no device table (θ and its inhomogeneity, mobility, residual ρ₀, gate dielectric thickness, channel geometry).

concerns.concern: The Methods omit the band-structure input used for the trigonal-warping velocity difference Δv_TW.
concerns.quote: The Methods give the screening-model integrals but omit the band-structure input for Δv_TW.

concerns.concern: Absorbed power, polarization and antenna coupling are not specified, which hinders reproducibility of the method by other groups.
concerns.quote: Specify the absorbed power and polarization and antenna coupling, so that other groups can reproduce the method

concerns.concern: The umklapp window is quoted as −3.5 < ν < 0.5 on a hole-side band, which is internally inconsistent and presumably should read −3.5 < ν < −0.5.
concerns.quote: "−3.5 < ν < 0.5 in a hole-side band", which is internally inconsistent (presumably −3.5 < ν < −0.5).

concerns.concern: Loose and inconsistent terminology (intervalley vs inter-pocket vs inter-layer), along with typos, obscures which collision process is meant.
concerns.quote: loose terminology (intervalley versus inter-pocket versus inter-layer) obscure which collision process is meant.

concerns.concern: Figure references in the main text are mismatched with the actual panels.
concerns.quote: "Fig. 1a shows transport data" should be Fig. 1c, and "Fig. 1b" for THz illumination should be Fig. 1d.
